mintAuthority.summary: STBT's controller enforces 24-hour implementation/issuer replacement and four-hour mint/rebase scheduling despite getMinDelay() returning zero. A separate reserve-feed owner can raise the reserve budget without a timelock. Native issuance is issuer-authorized, not atomically deposit-bound; financial reconciliation and supervisory controls remain unestablished.
mintAuthority.headline: Issuer minting has a four-hour delay, but a separate key can raise the reserve ceiling without delay.

review.evidence: Full controller RoleGranted/RoleRevoked/RoleAdminChanged replay from deployment through block 26110197 and hasRole checks resolve all current members: admin is the controller itself; proposers are 0x65ff5a67d8d7292bd4ea7b6cd863d9f3ca14f046 and 0xca241823d4bfe8b29610709db617407fbc9ae02b (verified user Minter); executor 0xd32a1441872774f30ec9c453983cf5c95a720123; canceller 0x520839e886a285e196c8fa3d161797b4bafabe94. The Minter owner is the executor EOA. Selector reads and verified override establish 86400s implementation/issuer replacement and 14400s issue/rebase/role changes. Issuer reserve budget remains mutable, so this is not immutable collateral gating. Organizational signing and financial reconciliation remain undisclosed. Organizational key-custody/independence of proposer, executor and canceller EOAs and current independent STBT reserve-to-liability reconciliation remain undisclosed. Sibling comparison on 2026-10-03: XAUm/XAGm's attestation-only supervision and periodic reconciliation cite Matrixdock's July 2026 Bureau Veritas physical gold/silver inventory verification and issuer-published token-supply comparison. That release explicitly extends the existing XAUm audit to XAGm for the first time and describes monthly reserve statements and on-chain proof of reserves for precious-metal products; it does not include STBT's Treasury/debt reserve book. STBT's public dashboard supplies issuer reserve NAV and asset composition, while its token-specific transparency documentation says underlying-asset reporting documents may be uploaded, not that the bullion attestation series covers STBT. Holding some BUIDL/USTB reserve assets likewise does not reconcile the whole STBT liability. No current STBT-specific recurring independent reserve/token-liability verification was established in the reviewed primary sources. Reconciliation and supervision therefore remain unknown, and the concentrated-admin posture is not promoted by borrowing the siblings' product-scoped assurance. D14/D29 sweep (2026-10-03): Verified STBT.issue(tokenHolder,value,data) is onlyIssuer and uses reserveFeed.latestRoundData as an issuer-reserve ceiling, not an atomic deposit/collateral-transfer requirement; the initial-supply branch also bypasses the reserve check. Existing pinned reviewed evidence identifies the issuer/owner controller and mutable reserve budget. The 14400-second selector-specific issue delay does not make issuance deposit-bound or economically capped against the controlling root. This is unbounded with reconciliation unknown, not D29 token governance. Pinned block hashes read this review: ethereum 26110197 0xa6bec96f66d0e4511728dd49fc828851fd28d75eb4b75dc24a2acfc9dec3cfd8. No transaction was sent; no governed-issuance qualification is claimed.

scopedQuestions.question: The issuer's March 18, 2023 whitepaper section 3.3.1 names Cactus custody for proposer/executor and self-hosted hardware wallets for canceller. This is a disclosed role-level custody model, not an MPC/HSM attestation or proof of independent humans for the currently identified proposer, executor and canceller EOAs. Are those historical custody arrangements still in force for the current role accounts, and which beneficial humans and approval policy govern them? The proposer Minter is owned by the identified executor EOA; verified role census and selector-specific timelock execution do not answer these off-chain questions.
